clue.text: Saddle and rope skilfully thrown over mammoth

parts.note: a col is a saddle, the low pass between two mountain peaks

indicators.note: turned over, so the rope's word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a lasso is a rope used with skill by a cowboy

explanation.surface: A cowboy deftly flings a saddle and lariat over a huge beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown' suits a lasso in the surface, but with 'over' it tells you to turn the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth used as an adjective means enormous, the same sense as colossal.

clue.text: Wary taking a drug abroad

parts.note: someone taking a drug is said to be on it

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller is nervous about carrying a drug in a foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on guard is to be watchful and alert to danger, which is what wary means.

clue.text: Buried treasure well recovered?

parts.note: the surface suggests a pirate's chest; the setter means a valuable resource lying underground
not someone back to health but a substance brought up from a drilled well

explanation.surface: A hoard of hidden treasure has been successfully dug up.
explanation.walkthrough: Petroleum, often called black gold, is the treasure buried underground and brought up from wells.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude petroleum is a precious resource found deep in the ground and extracted through drilled wells.

clue.text: Oscar puts on gloves, conversely making head warmer

indicators.note: the other way round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
used as a verb: the word for putting on wraps around the letter like a glove

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on
O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called Oscar dresses in gloves and, contrariwise, a hat for the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloves' looks like a noun for the hands, but it is a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A snood is a hood or close-fitting knitted tube worn over the head and neck for warmth.

clue.text: See paintbrush not yet in the bag

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or see
a sable is an artist's brush made from the fur of the animal

explanation.surface: An artist's brush is spotted but has not been packed away yet.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest not yet in the bag is not secured, so it could still be lost.

clue.text: Group of members decided on yearly fee

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a sub, short for subscription, is a membership fee paid each year
a set date is one that has been decided

explanation.surface: A club committee settles on what its annual subscription should be.
explanation.walkthrough: In mathematics a subset is a set whose elements all belong to a larger set.
explanation.definitionFit: A subset is a smaller collection drawn from within a larger body, as a committee is.

clue.text: Sorts regularly hiding horse inside mule?

definitions.text: Sorts regularly hiding horse inside mule?

indicators.note: the outer letters conceal the rest within them
taking letters at regular intervals: the first, third and fifth of the word

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of this word are kept

indicators.note: the horse goes into the middle of the animal's name

parts.note: a mule is also slang for a drug courier
gee-gee is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: People who conceal heroin (horse) inside a drug courier's body are exactly what the answer describes.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin and a mule is a courier who carries drugs, often internally, so the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Smugglers move contraband secretly, and drug mules hiding heroin are a classic type of them.

clue.text: Ridge poles set on new American houses

parts.note: a brow is the ridge or top of a hill
N and S, the north and south poles

indicators.note: the letters are made new by rearranging them

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Poles are fixed along a ridge to frame some new building.
explanation.walkthrough: The two poles sit at either end of the rearranged word. A brownstone is a New York town house faced with reddish-brown sandstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownstones are terraced town houses typical of New York, named after their sandstone facing.

clue.text: Serious organ music causes vibrations in home

parts.note: the ear is the organ whose drum vibrates when music is heard
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Solemn church organ music makes the whole house shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ music' reads as one phrase, but the organ is a body part described by the words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and solemn in intent, a close synonym of serious.

clue.text: Young lady downs bodily fluid, funny bad taste

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
downs and ups are lows and highs
in old medicine the four humours were the body's fluids

explanation.surface: A girl gulps down some body fluid, a joke in very poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downs' looks like a verb for drinking, but it is a noun meaning low points.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallows humour is grim joking about death or disaster, comedy that can seem tasteless.

clue.text: Arabic name African prince tried to keep secret

parts.note: ras is an Ethiopian title for a prince or chief
to have hidden something is to have tried to keep it secret

explanation.surface: A prince from Africa attempted to conceal his Arab name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashid is a common Arabic given name, meaning rightly guided.

clue.text: Hot shifting some pianos, the upright type

indicators.note: moving the letters about into a new arrangement, as removal men shift furniture

parts.note: these words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Moving pianos is sweaty work, especially the upright kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' looks like a piano type, but it means walking erect.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern humans are the species that stands and walks erect, so they are the upright kind.

clue.text: Ask private, one just embarking

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
inner thoughts are private ones

explanation.surface: A soldier is asked about being a raw recruit just starting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier, but it is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is a novice, someone just starting out on a new activity.

clue.text: Crashpad a man developed protects fallers

indicators.note: the outer words shelter the answer within them

parts.note: the answer runs across these words, from the end of the first to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A climber's crash mat, built by someone, keeps those who fall safe.
explanation.walkthrough: A crashpad is a mat protecting a climber who falls; the setter's fallers are the pair expelled from Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man and woman in Genesis are known for the Fall, when they disobeyed God.

clue.text: Relation arrived wanting mother to provide accommodation

indicators.note: giving lodging, so one word houses the other inside it

parts.note: a mother tongue or country is one's native one
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrived

explanation.surface: A relative turns up, needing their mother to put them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' is not family here but a telling of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is an account or story, and a narrative is a recounting of events.

clue.text: Carry child back from playdate

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the back of the word, its final letter

parts.note: only the final letter of this word is used

explanation.surface: A parent has to carry a toddler home from a playdate.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to lug or haul something, an informal synonym of carry.

clue.text: Likely winners missing start of Ascot, perhaps

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Ascot is a famous horse-racing course, so it suggests races

explanation.surface: Tipped horses fail to turn up for the beginning of the Ascot meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, England, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are top performers, the ones expected to win a contest.

clue.text: Cold drink for each bell ringer?

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A chilly beverage is handed to every member of a bell-ringing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bell ringer' suggests a campanologist, but it is the tongue inside the bell that strikes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The clapper is the swinging metal tongue that strikes a bell to make it ring.

clue.text: Covering chest, sensor bespoke good health

indicators.note: one set of letters is wrapped around the other
made to order, so the letters are refashioned

parts.note: this word supplies the letters to be rearranged
a bust is the chest, especially a woman's

explanation.surface: A custom-made sensor strapped over the chest tracks someone's fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bespoke' reads as tailored hardware, but signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Robustness is strength and sturdiness of body, which amounts to vigorous good health.

clue.text: Habitual complainer wants bill voided by diner

indicators.note: emptied out, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of this word are kept
a diner is someone who eats

explanation.surface: A grumbling diner insists that the restaurant bill be cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voided' sounds like cancelling a bill, but it means emptying the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleater is a whiner who keeps moaning, like a bleating sheep.

clue.text: Briefly view apartment block in Manhattan, the lower part

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to see something is to view it
condo is the American word for a block of owned flats

explanation.surface: A quick look round a New York flat on one of its lower floors.
explanation.walkthrough: In a piano duet, the secondo plays the lower part while the primo takes the upper.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondo is the musical term for the bass half of a piano duet, the lower part.

clue.text: Fighter switched crude strategy after four failures, perhaps

indicators.note: turned round, so the word runs back to front

parts.note: raw means unrefined, as crude oil is
after Plans A, B, C and D fail, you reach Plan E

explanation.surface: A boxer abandons a rough game plan after losing four bouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' suggests a boxer, but it is an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter is a fast military aircraft designed for combat, a type of warplane.

clue.text: Simple things like ballpoint pens and spades

parts.note: Bic is the brand name of a famous ballpoint pen
as means like, in the sense of in the manner of

explanation.surface: Basic objects such as biros and garden spades.
explanation.walkthrough: The comparison word sits inside the pen brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Basics are the fundamentals or essentials, the simplest items one needs.

clue.text: Bishop on bicycle, last to arrive for service

parts.note: to ride is what you do on a bike

explanation.surface: A bishop cycles in, the final person to reach church for the service.
explanation.walkthrough: The bride traditionally arrives last at her wedding service.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding ceremony the woman getting married customarily enters after all the guests.

clue.text: Baby expert backed scheme to impregnate hereditary peer

indicators.note: to fill or permeate, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a patrician is an aristocrat by birth

indicators.note: reversed, read back to front

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A child doctor supported a plan to get an aristocrat pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like support for the scheme, but it signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A paediatrician is a doctor specialising in children, so an expert in babies.

clue.text: Mark permanently a little sunburned without cap

indicators.note: losing its top, the first letter in a down answer

parts.note: skin turned pink is mildly sunburned

explanation.surface: Getting slightly burnt without a hat leaves a lasting mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without cap' suits a sun hat, but it means dropping the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink is to tattoo, marking the skin permanently.

clue.text: Parisian's salad French? That's understood

parts.note: I see is the phrase for showing you understand

explanation.surface: A Parisian orders a salad and the waiter answers that he understands.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisée is curly endive, a frilly salad leaf named with the French word for curled.

clue.text: Maybe skipper's binding Essex's opener into playing for Kent

indicators.note: the letters are played with, set out in a new order
the opening letter of the word

parts.note: only the first letter of this word is used
these words supply most of the letters to be rearranged
